quote: Foundation Medicine was founded in 2010 by Todd Golub, Levi Garraway and Eric Lander.
reason: the founding trio; every distractor is a real founding trio of another company in the dossier (Beam, Alnylam, CRISPR Therapeutics), so a wrong answer teaches a second entry

quote: At the time of founding, Eric Lander was director of the Broad Institute and a professor at Harvard Medical School and MIT, Todd Golub was founding director of the Broad Institute's Cancer Program at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, and Levi Garraway was an assistant professor of medicine in medical oncology at Dana-Farber.
reason: the lineage matters more than the names — it is the network the Izar and Azizi connections already run through; distractors are three other real Boston institution pairs

quote: Roche acquired Foundation Medicine in 2018 and has operated it as a subsidiary since.
reason: acquirer and year together, so neither can be guessed from the other; distractors are plausible tools-and-diagnostics acquirers at varied years, deliberately not all clustered on one date

quote: Before the Roche acquisition the company had raised approximately $96.5 million across four rounds from thirteen investors.
reason: a total raised is normally volatile because it goes up, but this one is frozen by the acquisition and can never change; distractors are the real totals of Nabla, Cellarity and Lila

quote: Daniel Malarek has been chief executive officer since 2023.
reason: distractors are three sitting Boston biotech CEOs from the dossier (Quanterix, Cellarity, Generate); this is the card most likely to go stale first, which is why people cards carry the shortest recheck expectation

quote: Foundation Medicine performs comprehensive genomic profiling of tumours to guide targeted therapy selection and clinical trial matching.
reason: asks for the pair rather than the category, because trial matching is the non-obvious half; asking what the company does in general would be answerable from the name

quote: FoundationOne CDx is the company's comprehensive genomic profiling test and companion diagnostic, providing information for five tumour types: ovarian, lung, breast, colorectal and melanoma.
reason: the specific five, not the fact that it profiles tumours; distractors are plausible five-cancer lists of the same shape

quote: FoundationOne Heme is the assay for haematologic malignancies and sarcomas.
reason: the sarcoma half is the surprising part of a product named Heme; distractors are other real assay scopes

quote: The liquid biopsy line has been sold as FoundationACT and later as FoundationOne Liquid.
reason: product naming is durable and is the kind of thing that comes up in an interview; distractors are invented but plausible Foundation-prefixed pairs, deliberately not real FM products so none is accidentally defensible

quote: In April 2026 Roche entered into a definitive merger agreement to acquire SAGA Diagnostics, whose tumour-informed molecular residual disease platform will be fully integrated into Foundation Medicine once the transaction closes.
reason: the target and what it adds; the Akoya distractor is true of Quanterix and the Olink one of Thermo Fisher, so both are swapped-company rather than invented

quote: The SAGA transaction was expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 at the latest.
reason: separates the timing from the deal itself so q10 cannot cue it; the hedge 'at the latest' is preserved because the source hedges

quote: Garrett Frampton is vice president and lead of the Computational Discovery group within research and development.
reason: the single most useful name in this deck — it is the group a computational hire would join; two distractors are real Lila Sciences titles, one is invented but plausible

quote: The Computational Discovery group conducts early-stage research on cancer genomics, computational pathology and clinical outcomes for patients.
reason: what the group actually works on, which is the part that maps onto the current job; distractors are three adjacent functions that exist at a diagnostics company and are not this group's remit

quote: The Computational Biology team is an interdisciplinary group comprised of computational biologists, molecular biologists, software engineers and other skilled specialists who work to enhance understanding of next-generation sequencing.
reason: the software-engineering half is the reason this company fits a comp-bio-plus-production-engineering profile specifically; distractors are three other plausible team compositions

quote: Foundation Medicine is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and posts senior computational biologist roles in the Boston area.
reason: location gates the commute and therefore the housing decision; all three distractors are real headquarters towns of other dossier companies (Generate/Cellarity, Dyno, Quanterix), so the card teaches the map

quote: Molecular residual disease testing detects cancer remaining after treatment, and adds longitudinal monitoring to a portfolio that was previously built around profiling a tumour once.
reason: dropped: what MRD testing detects is sector-level knowledge true of every MRD assay, not a fact about Foundation Medicine. The company-specific half — that Roche is buying the platform — is already q10. Leaves f11 reported as uncovered, which is correct.

quote: The company has over 1,700 employees across locations in North America and Germany.
reason: dropped: headcount is volatile by definition. Extracted so the research is complete and so a later pass can see it was considered; carding it would assert a number that is wrong within two quarters and the reader could not tell.
